Left fusion_v2_enabled=false, fusion_v2_auto_promote=true as required.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/topology.py _apply_vm_parents: correctly re-parents both managed VMs (hyperv_host_ip or virtual MAC OUI on same FDB port) and discovered_endpoint nodes with virtual MAC on same switch port as a managed server. The 'kept' filter (line 72) prunes ONLY switch->vm edges when a different host is chosen; if the switch itself would have been the host it would incorrectly keep both — not an issue in practice because switches are never in server_ips.

alert_engine.fusion_promotion_status: agree_pct is computed on ALL logs (even down-then-up UP-recovery rows) — as long as _write_fusion_shadow_log only writes real KO cases this is fine, but any future call from a non-KO branch would inflate the denominator.

alert_engine.maybe_promote_fusion_v2: writes fusion_v2_promoted_at + fusion_v2_promoted_reason, but does NOT update the in-memory routes/fusion._cache — the /api/fusion/certainty page can show stale 'enabled=false' for up to 60s after auto-promotion. Same caveat as iter151 (config cache invalidation).

routes/topology.get_switch_ports: attached[] correctly labels mac_oui devices with '<Vendor> device' — for Hyper-V it becomes 'Microsoft Hyper-V device' which matches the frontend expectation; still relies on a static VIRTUAL_OUI list (no fallback to IEEE OUI DB), which is acceptable given the small set of virt vendors.

Seeding remains fragile: PC-MARIO datto document is periodically overwritten by the datto poller; iter151 report already flags this. Re-running seed_fusion_iter151.py just before tests is the current workaround.
